result.topic_en: Gauss works with the hypergeometric differential equation: he derives the Wronskian-type relation for two solutions, derives Euler's transformation F(α,β,γ) = (1−x)^{γ−α−β} F(γ−α,γ−β,γ), and lists contiguous relations useful for continued fractions.
result.transcription:
$\alpha\beta P - \gamma(1-2x)\frac{dP}{dx} [-+-] - (x-xx)\frac{ddP}{dx^2} = 0$
$\alpha\beta Q - \gamma(1-2x)\frac{dQ}{dx} [-+-] - (x-xx)\frac{ddQ}{dx^2} = 0$
Hieraus folgt
$-\frac{\gamma(1-2x)dx}{x-xx} = \frac{Qd^2P - Pd^2Q}{QdP - PdQ}$
also
[31] $Q\frac{dP}{dx} - P\frac{dQ}{dx} = A(x-xx)^{-\gamma}$
wo $A$ eine Constante ist, deren Werth weiterhin zu
$\frac{\alpha.\beta.\ \alpha+1.\beta+1.\ \alpha+2.\beta+2}{\gamma\ .\ \gamma.\gamma+1\ .\ \gamma+1.\gamma+2}$ ... bestimmt wird.
Also z. B. für $\alpha=\frac{1}{2}, \beta=\frac{1}{2}, \gamma=1$
$A = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{8}\cdot\frac{25}{24}\cdot\frac{49}{48}\cdot\ldots\ldots = \frac{1}{\pi}$
Dieselbe kann auch durch {+allgemein+}
$\frac{\alpha\beta}{\gamma}\left[1 + \frac{\gamma-\alpha.\gamma-\beta}{1.\gamma+1} + \frac{\gamma-\alpha.\gamma+1-\alpha.\ \gamma-\beta.\gamma+1-\beta}{1.\ 2.\ \ \gamma+1.\gamma+2} + \text{etc.}\right]$ vorgestellt werden

Eine der merkwürdigsten Relationen finden wir auf folgende Art:
Man setze $P = P'(1-x)^{\mu}$, so wird obige Differentialgleichung
$\left(\alpha\beta + \frac{\mu(\gamma-(\alpha+\beta+\mu)x)}{1-x}\right)P' - (\gamma-(\alpha+\beta+2\mu+1)x)\frac{dP'}{dx} - (x-xx)\frac{d^2P'}{dx^2} [-=0-] = 0$
Man setze $\mu = \gamma-\alpha-\beta$, so wird diese Gleichung
$(\gamma-\alpha)(\gamma-\beta)P' - (\gamma-(2\gamma-\alpha-\beta+1)x)\frac{dP'}{dx} - (x-xx)\frac{d^2P'}{dx^2} = 0$
woraus leicht folgt
$P' = F(\gamma-\alpha, \gamma-\beta, \gamma)$, also
[32] $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = (1-x)^{-\alpha[-+-]-\beta+\gamma} F(\gamma-\alpha,\gamma-\beta,\gamma)$
Zur Verwandlung unsrer Functionen oder ihrer Verhältnisse in continuirliche Brüche sind folgende Relationen brauchbar:
[33] $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma+1) - F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = -\frac{\alpha\beta x}{\gamma.\gamma+1}F(\alpha+1,\beta+1,\gamma+2)$
[34] $F(\alpha,\beta+1,\gamma) - F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = \frac{\alpha x}{\gamma}F(\alpha+1,\beta+1,\gamma+1)$
[35] $F(\alpha+1,\beta,\gamma) - F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = \frac{\beta x}{\gamma}F(\alpha+1,\beta+1,\gamma+1)$

methods.what: Hypergeometric differential equation satisfied by two solutions P and Q (as written on the page)
Eliminating αβ between the two equations gives a logarithmic-derivative relation for the Wronskian
Wronskian of two solutions equals a constant times (x−x²)^{−γ}
Infinite product for the constant A; for α=β=1/2, γ=1 it equals 1/π
General series expression for the constant A
Substitution P = P'(1−x)^μ transforms the differential equation

methods.what: Choosing μ = γ−α−β gives again a hypergeometric equation with parameters γ−α, γ−β, γ
